roadmap_item: APO-7 (7. E04/E06 持久触发与失败恢复)

contract: state: fixed schema, unknown fields and duplicate JSON keys rejected, exit 2
queue/state/audit budgets: 4MiB each, queue <=4096 triggers, candidate and platform files <=1MiB
persistent_trigger: enqueue appends canonical line to queue.jsonl with fsync, exit 0
duplicate id with identical content -> exit 0 action=duplicate-noop, zero write
same id with different content -> exit 1 action=conflict-frozen, zero write
one seq bound to two ids -> exit 1 action=conflict-frozen, zero write
ordering policy is explicit: admission is append-only and never sorts or drops a late trigger; the consumer is strict FIFO and never skips a gap
lock: state.lease = {holder, token, expires_at}; token is a monotonic fencing generation
live lease held by another holder -> exit 1 action=lease-held, zero write
caller lease token != current generation -> exit 1 action=stale-lease
job recorded under an older lease generation -> exit 1 action=stale-lease (fencing)
expired lease is taken over with token+1; .durable-trigger.lock is a separate process mutex
cursor: state.cursor_seq starts at -1 and advances only on a successful apply
only the trigger at cursor_seq+1 is consumed; strict FIFO, gaps are never skipped
a gap at the cursor -> exit 1 action=out-of-order-rejected with expected_seq, missing_seq, next_available_seq
consumed ids are recorded; re-firing a consumed id -> exit 0 action=duplicate-noop
same id repeated in the queue is consumed exactly once
restart_continuation: a failed apply leaves the job at APPLY_PENDING with before_sha256 and before_present
the next trigger resumes the pending job when it sits at the cursor
resume re-checks the target bytes against the recorded before_sha256; mismatch -> exit 1 action=conflict-frozen
atomic_apply: apply order: lease -> fencing -> kill switch -> approval -> candidate digest -> other bots -> target drift -> record before-state -> atomic replace -> platform readback -> other bots again -> state -> audit
atomic replace = temp file -> fsync -> rename -> fsync directory
approval records the candidate byte digest; candidate bytes changed after approval -> exit 1 action=stale-candidate
readback re-reads the target file and compares SHA256 to the candidate digest; mismatch -> atomic restore, exit 1 action=readback-mismatch, never reports applied
other_bots_unchanged: every baselined bot other than the target is compared before and after the apply
a drifted bot or a bot outside the baseline -> exit 1 action=other-bot-changed, zero apply
a drift detected after the apply -> atomic restore of the target, exit 1 action=other-bot-changed
failure_recovery: approval-missing, stale-candidate, baseline-missing, readback-mismatch, other-bot-changed, injected failure, stale-lease -> job status APPLY_PENDING, never 'applied'
rollback restores the pre-apply bytes atomically and verifies the readback; mismatch -> exit 1 action=rollback-failed
rollback of a never-applied job -> exit 1 action=rollback-unavailable; second rollback -> exit 0 action=already-rolled-back
kill-switch --engage blocks new applies (exit 1 action=kill-switch-engaged) but still allows rollback
audit: append-only audit.jsonl records apply, refuse, rollback, approve, baseline and kill-switch events
each entry carries timestamp, action, trigger id, seq, target bot, result, digests and lease generation
verify: read-only consistency check across state, queue, platform and audit
detects duplicate queue ids, consumed ids without a job, APPLIED jobs without after_sha256, platform drift, unknown and missing bots
exit 0 verdict=PASS scope=state-queue-platform-audit-bytes-only; exit 1 verdict=FAIL with problems
cli: --version prints v1 and the sha256 of this capability README without reading any input
exit 0 = completed per contract, 1 = runtime rejection, 2 = usage and contract errors
